title: Finite-order residue-trivial DVR automorphisms in residue characteristic zero
statement: Let $C$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and residue field $\kappa=C/\mathfrak m$ of characteristic zero. Let $t$ be a uniformizer. Let $a:C\xrightarrow{\sim}C$ be a ring automorphism of finite order: $a^N=\mathrm{id}_C$ for some integer $N>0$. Suppose $a(c)-c\in\mathfrak m$ for every $c\in C$, and $a(t)/t-1\in\mathfrak m$, where $a(t)/t$ is a unit of $C$. Then $a=\mathrm{id}_C$.

source.place: Tag 09EE, lemma-galois-inertia, proof of (3): the telescoping sum for a finite-order automorphism acting trivially on every associated-graded piece, specialized to residue characteristic zero; the proof uses only these displayed automorphism hypotheses, not a Galois extension.

proof.text: By [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $\mathfrak m=tC$, so $\mathfrak m^i=t^iC$ for every $i\geq0$. Write $a(t)=vt$ with $v\in C^\times$ and $v-1\in\mathfrak m$. For $x=t^i b\in\mathfrak m^i$, the identity $a(x)-x=t^i((v^i-1)a(b)+(a(b)-b))$ shows $a(x)-x\in\mathfrak m^{i+1}$: both terms in parentheses lie in $\mathfrak m$, using $v^i-1=(v-1)(1+v+\cdots+v^{i-1})$ when $i>0$ and $v^0-1=0$ when $i=0$. In particular $a(\mathfrak m^i)\subseteq\mathfrak m^i$.

proof.text: For every $i\geq0$, $x\in\mathfrak m^i$, and $j\geq0$, we have $a^j(x)-x\in\mathfrak m^{i+1}$. Indeed it is zero for $j=0$; and $a^{j+1}(x)-x=(a(a^j(x))-a^j(x))+(a^j(x)-x)$ lies in $\mathfrak m^{i+1}$ by Step 1 and the induction hypothesis, since Step 1 also keeps every $a^j(x)$ in $\mathfrak m^i$.
